text:
Maya Patel: Heads up — we’re seeing a spike in failed provisioning jobs in us-west-3 after last night’s node maintenance. ~18% of new GPU allocs are failing with kernel attach errors and several BMCs flipped secure-boot to enabled unexpectedly. Can someone with OOB access glance?
Arjun Singh: I’m seeing BMC sessions drop during flash finalization. ipmitool logs show lots of "Unable to establish IPMI v2 session" around 02:13 UTC. Also a few nodes report UEFI variable mismatch: "SecureBoot: state changed (0 -> 1)".
provision-bot: [automated] provisioning-failures/us-west-3: 182 failed (rolling 10m), 14% failure rate, top errors: gpu-attach, nvram-mismatch.
deploy-bot: Completed firmware push to us-west-3 (fw-v2.7.3 -> fw-v2.8.0) at 02:00 UTC. No rollback executed.
Ken Walters: Thanks — that deploy correlates. My suspicion: fw-v2.8.0 toggles a UEFI variable on some BMCs when NV storage has bit flips. If SecureBoot flips we need manual accept or NVRAM sync. Repro steps: flash image -> reboot -> uefi reports variable mismatch -> secureboot toggles.
Lina Gomez: Capacity-wise this is starting to affect jobs. Scheduler reports 22 queued GPU-heavy jobs waiting; cost bump as we spill to on-demand clusters in other regions. Suggest temporary routing policy to divert new heavy GPU jobs to eu-west while we fix canary. @sre-oncall can you approve? :eyes:
sre-oncall: Approving temporary routing change to route new high-memory GPU jobs from us-west-3 -> eu-west-1. Make sure we tag affected racks so Dedicated pools don't get auto-filled.
Arjun Singh: Quick troubleshooting note — on one affected host I did: 
```
# show last uefi vars
sudo dmidecode -t 11 | grep -i secure
journalctl -u fw-update -b | tail -n 60
ipmitool sol payload on
```
The ipmi SOL shows the firmware asking to confirm vars after reboot but our OOB automation isn’t sending the keystrokes so it stays in a pending state.
Maya Patel: Ok I'm going to kick a targeted rollback on the two most impacted racks (rack-usw3-17, rack-usw3-18) as a canary. Plan: 1) drain rack, 2) power-cycle via BMC, 3) flash fw-v2.7.3, 4) validate NV-RAM and kernel attach, 5) un-drain. Posting runbook excerpt below.
Maya Patel: Runbook snippet ->
```
# drain
scheduler drain-rack --id rack-usw3-17 --grace 300
# power-cycle via BMC
for host in $(list-hosts rack-usw3-17); do ipmitool -H $host -U admin -P **** chassis power off; sleep 6; ipmitool -H $host -U admin -P **** chassis power on; done
# flash rollback
fwtool flash --image fw-v2.7.3 --targets rack-usw3-17 --verify
# validate
fwtool nvram-check --rack rack-usw3-17 || echo "nvram mismatch"
# re-enable
scheduler undrain-rack --id rack-usw3-17
```
Ken Walters: If anyone has physical access on-call please stand by for a couple of boards that may fail the automated SOL flow — we may need to attach a serial cable for manual variable acceptance.
Arjun Singh: I’ll take rack-usw3-17 canary. I’ll also patch OOB automation to send the ESC/Enter sequence if UEFI prompt seen. Pushing a short-lived script to the runbook agent now.
Maya Patel: Update 2165432145 — first two canary nodes in rack-usw3-17 back online after rollback, GPUs reattached, nvram-check passes. Failure rate in us-west-3 down to 4% and scheduler queue draining. Will monitor for 30m then schedule wider rollback if stable. Thanks everyone :high_voltage:
Ken Walters: Nice work. Once stable let's add fw-v2.8.0 to the hardware-compat matrix and disable the automatic NVRAM toggle, or require explicit opt-in.
Lina Gomez: I'll keep routing rule in place for 1h and notify sales/support about potential job delays.
provision-bot: [automated] provisioning-failures/us-west-3: 62 failed (rolling 10m), 3.9% failure rate.
